comment: Blamsoft publish no source. The two unlabelled jacks in the MIX row are settled by the panel's own connector artwork, which draws a line from the left jack up to the mode display and from the right jack across to the MIX knob: input 3 is read as mode = display mode + int(v*3.5 + 0.5) clamped to 0-35, and input 4 as mix = knob + 0.1v clamped to 0-1. The frequency jack is tagged pitch: the cutoff runs 20Hz to 20000Hz over the knob's full travel and 10V covers that travel with the attenuverter open, which is 9.97 octaves for 10V, so it tracks a volt per octave to within a third of a semitone over the full 10V. The manual's MIX paragraph is copied verbatim from the XFX Reverb manual and describes an LFO; the code blends dry input against filtered output. The manual also describes comb, FM, RM and bitcrusher modes as non-traditional additions, and all four are present in this build. The widget adds no context menu of its own; the filter-mode submenus (Sallen-Key, State Variable, Ladder, Dual Resonator, Comb) belong to the mode display's own menu, which the note above says is opened by clicking the display. The maker's PDF manual was read on this pass with pypdf; it supplied the slope-per-pole convention and the account of the comb, FM, RM and bitcrusher modes, which it groups as non-traditional. All 36 mode names are present, FM and RM included.
